newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - April 28.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - April 28.

text.p: Bolger steers clear of super row: Prime Minister Jim Bolger will not stick his neck out over a bid by Treasurer Winston Peters -- opposed by some National MPs -- to have the compulsory superannuation scheme entrenched by legislation if it is passed by referendum. Page 1.
Labour seeks to regain Maori support: Labour's battle to woo back Maori voters dominated debate during the party's Wellington regional conference. Page 2.
Creech wavers on student allowances: Education Minister Wyatt Creech cannot guarantee that universal living allowances will be introduced for tertiary students. Page 2.
English taking hard line on CHEs: The government intends to take a hard line on extra money for hospitals claiming revenue problems, Health Minister Bill English has said. Page 2.
Parliament 'palace' on Cabinet agenda: The future of the $94 million proposed ministerial building is back on the Cabinet's agenda today. Page 2.

Moore says government should back Dairy Board: Labour MP and former trade minister Mike Moore on Sunday renewed demands for the government to go in to bat for the Dairy Board after six board officials in Europe were arrested on fraud charges. Page 2.

Confidence slips across all sectors: Business confidence has fallen since the formation of the Coalition Government and positive signs of economic growth are "few and far between," according to the Institute of Economic Research. Page 12.

Lyttelton sales: Two Canterbury district councils sold their shares in Lyttelton Port Company on Wednesday. The Waimakariri and Banks Peninsula district councils sold their shares to AMP Investments (NZ). Page 12.
'Horrific' road toll for the holiday: Observance of basic road safety rules would have prevented the "horrific" number of road deaths over the holiday weekend.
CBD hoping to raise $29.5m: Auckland-based property investor CBD NZ hopes to raise between $19.5 million and $29.5 million through an issue of $1 shares.

Govt likely to approve 'palace': Lavish building to go ahead despite controversy: Government plans to release costings to justify cabinet approval today for spending of nearly $100 million on a new building in Wellington.
Strong kiwi eats price gains: The continuing strength of the New Zealand dollar limited gains from stronger world commodity prices during March ANZ says.
Market spread for butter sought: The Dairy Board is looking at marked opportunities for its spreadable butter in both Australia and Chile, says a director, Richard Booth.
